units.label: 1(a)
units.summary: Describe what an integrated development environment is.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of a definition.

units.label: 1(b)
units.summary: Identify and describe three IDE features that help programmers find bugs.
units.difficulty_basis: 6 marks; three features each identified and described.

units.label: 2(a)
units.summary: Identify the parameter passed to the queue add procedure.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark identification from given code.

units.label: 2(b)
units.summary: Describe the logical decision made in the add-to-queue algorithm.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark interpretation of a condition in given code.

units.label: 2(c)(i)
units.summary: Explain the logic mistake in the algorithm that adds an item to a queue.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark reasoning about pointer misuse in a queue operation.

units.label: 2(c)(ii)
units.summary: Rewrite the add-to-queue algorithm to correct the mistake.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark correction of queue pointer handling.

units.label: 3(a)
units.summary: Describe one difference between a global and a local variable.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of scope definitions.

units.label: 3(b)
units.summary: Explain with an example why global variables are sometimes used.
units.difficulty_basis: 3 marks; explanation plus a suitable example.

units.label: 3(c)
units.summary: Explain why good practice generally avoids global variables.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark explanation of drawbacks of global scope.

units.label: 3(d)
units.summary: Explain why passing parameters can be better than using global variables.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark explanation relating parameters to side effects.

units.label: 4(a)
units.summary: Describe what a function is.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of a definition.

units.label: 4(b)
units.summary: Compare a procedure with a function.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark comparison of two subroutine types.

units.label: 4(c)(i)
units.summary: Identify two other functions used in the given code besides the user-defined ones.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark identification from given code.

units.label: 4(c)(ii)
units.summary: State the output of the given code for the input 3.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark routine trace of short code.

units.label: 4(d)
units.summary: Discuss reasons why a company enforces standard rules on how functions are written.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark extended response needing application of several rules to context.

units.label: 5(a)
units.summary: Identify four inputs for the engine management feature and suggest a data type for each.
units.difficulty_basis: 8 marks; inputs and types from an unfamiliar scenario.

units.label: 5(b)
units.summary: Identify two outputs from the engine management feature.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark identification from a scenario.

units.label: 5(c)
units.summary: Write an algorithm for the engine stop-start feature with several overriding conditions.
units.difficulty_basis: 8-mark original algorithm with endless loop and multiple combined conditions in an unfamiliar scenario.

units.label: 6(a)
units.summary: Explain why the developers need to use abstraction.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark explanation of the need for abstraction in a scenario.

units.label: 6(b)(i)
units.summary: State two similarities between the virtual and real town and explain why each exists.
units.difficulty_basis: 4 marks; identification plus explanation in context.

units.label: 6(b)(ii)
units.summary: State two differences between the virtual and real town.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark identification of abstraction differences.

units.label: 6(c)
units.summary: Describe how the simulator would check the driver obeys a no overtaking sign.
units.difficulty_basis: 3-mark description of decision logic for a scenario.
